title: A project detail couples a skill to one project
caption: A project detail written into a skill ties it to that one project.

coupling.question: is it tied to one place?
coupling.head: A project detail written into the skill
coupling.text: <marker>True at site 4, wrong at site 7: the AI follows the skill to the letter, and the dive still fails.</marker>

coding.head: A hard-coded path in a skill
coding.text: In a benchmark of 98 public skills, a workflow template made the agent write to .github/workflows/ when the task asked for ci/.

pointer.head: Code has a word for this: coupling.
pointer.text: <marker>The fewer and simpler the connections between modules, the easier each is to understand (Stevens, Myers and Constantine, 1974). Written for code modules, applied to skills by analogy.</marker>

analogy: At site 7 the seabed lies at 120 m; the card still says 40.

alt.dives: One skill card pinned above two dives. At site 4 the robot reaches the seabed at 40 m. At site 7 the seabed lies at 120 m, and the robot following the same card hangs at 40 m, 80 m short.

coupling-as-first-written.description: "The fewer and simpler the connections between modules, the easier it is to understand each module without reference to other modules" [1]. It is a design principle for code modules, applied to skills by analogy.

structured-design.title: Stevens, Myers and Constantine, Structured design

project-details-hard-coded-into-a-skill-.header: Project details hard-coded into a skill can override the task
project-details-hard-coded-into-a-skill-.description: In a benchmark of 98 public skills, a generic workflow template made the agent write files to .github/workflows/ when the task required ci/; the authors advise abstract guidance over templates with hard-coded paths [1]. It is one worked example, not a test of this picture.

swe-skills-bench.title: Han et al., SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?

scribbled-in.title: Scribbled in
scribbled-in.script: Take a sampling skill with one project detail written into it: "descend to 40 metres", true at site 4. At site 7 the seabed lies at 120, and the robot hangs uselessly at 40 while the model follows the skill perfectly. (pause) The skill was followed to the letter, and the dive still failed.

coupling.title: Coupling
coupling.script: Engineers have a word for this mistake: coupling. The 40 metres written into the skill ties it to one place. For a skill it comes down to this: keep project details out, so the skill has no ties to one project.
